source.description:
PROBLEM
Every description of the dispatch contract — the tool parameter text on both frontends, the planning skill, CLAUDE.md, the bead template — calls it the 7-section contract and then appends 'plus a SCRUTINY level'. The gate requires eight things. SCRUTINY is named last, outside the count, in every place a writer looks.

The result is measurable rather than theoretical. Audited every open bead on this epic with evaluateBeadReadiness on 2026-09-08: FOUR contracts hand-written by the coordinator omitted SCRUTINY and would have been refused at dispatch — a live operator probe bead (refused live, in a real pi session), and epic beads .36, .30 and .39. Four out of four. None was caught by reading; all were caught by running the gate.

This is the same shape as unitAI-rrdnt.54 one layer out. There the tool description named the sections and never stated the format the parser required; here it states a count that is wrong by one, and the omitted item is exactly the one outside the count.

SUCCESS
A writer following any description of the contract produces something the gate admits. The count and the requirement agree.

SCRUTINY
LOW

SCOPE
The wording wherever the contract is described: both frontends' tool parameter text, the planning skill, CLAUDE.md's dispatch section, and any bead template. Not the gate — the gate is right.

NON_GOALS
Does not make SCRUTINY optional. Does not change which sections are required. Does not change the refusal shape.

CONSTRAINTS
Do not fix this by making the gate lenient. SCRUTINY drives reviewer escalation on sensitive surfaces and a contract without it is genuinely underspecified — the requirement is correct and only its description is wrong.
Whatever the new wording is, it must be the SAME on both frontends. Divergent wording between the two is the failure documented in .55 and .56.

VALIDATION
Every place that describes the contract states the same count, and that count matches what evaluateBeadReadiness enforces.

OUTPUT
The corrected wording, and a note on the audit method: run the gate over the board rather than reading beads, because reading is what missed this four times.
source.notes:
PARTLY DONE 2026-09-08. Both frontends now state the valid SCRUTINY levels verbatim (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL) and say EIGHT required parts rather than seven — landed in b3c98a1e after an operator hit exactly this, inventing 'normal' and burning a dispatch.

REMAINING: the phrase '7-section contract' still appears in config/skills/using-specialists/SKILL.md and CLAUDE.md. Those are what a coordinator reads BEFORE it ever sees a tool description, so they are the earlier point of failure and the bead is not done.
source.title: The '7-section contract' actually requires eight things, and SCRUTINY is the one always dropped
